title: .issues/prisma-setup.md
B1 — Populate `card_concepts`, or formally retire Concept
description:
Blocking issue from `trope-cards/docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §8 B1. Decision recorded in §12 Q2.

## Problem

`card_concepts` exists in the schema (2 FKs + PK) and `seed/index.ts` inserts the 6 `concepts`
rows, but there is **no `cardConcepts` insert anywhere in the codebase** and `CardSeed` has no
`concepts` field. All 6 concepts are therefore orphaned: a Concept node in any view has no edge to
any card.

This is why the v1 `card-argument-taxonomy` view emits no Concept nodes. Emitting them anyway would
require inventing the edges, i.e. authoring ontology inside a projection.

## Interaction

`mechanisms` and `concepts` share slugs on `collectivisation` and `racial-essentialism` — two
tables, two independent `UNIQUE(slug)` constraints, near-duplicate definitions. Populating
`card_concepts` forces a decision on which table owns those two slugs. Per
`docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §9, that collision has been deferred until this issue is addressed.

## Options

1. Populate `card_concepts` from the authored corpus: add a `concepts` field to `CardSeed`, insert
   the link rows with a `relationship` value, resolve the two slug collisions, then add an
   integration test asserting no concept is orphaned.
2. Formally retire Concept: drop the `concepts`/`card_concepts` tables in a migration and remove
   the node type from the view registry.

Option 1 is cheaper and preserves the ontology the ADR already commits to. Option 2 is more honest if
Concept was never actually meant to be used.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decision is recorded in `docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §11 Q2.
- Every `concepts` row has at least one `card_concepts` row, **or** the tables are dropped.
- The slug collision on `collectivisation` and `racial-essentialism` is resolved, not left ambiguous.
- `verify-seed.ts` covers `card_concepts` so the state is checked by the seed gate.
- The projection view registry is updated accordingly, and the exclusion warning disappears.
- No second ontology is introduced to hold the answer.
close_reason: Resolved in 1476558 (Concept projection path) plus f00e430 (corpus increment). card_concepts is authored and seeded: 12 rows across 11 cards, 4 concepts (the 2 evidence-tier concepts were retired as orphans in the D1 decision). Reader expands card_concepts into Concept nodes and claim links; taxonomy emits Concept while card-argument-taxonomy excludes it by scope. Verified in production 2026-10-05: trope_graph.card_concepts=12, concepts=4, and /api/graph/views returns 200 with the Concept nodes present. Reports: issue #3 comments 5996397486 and 5997521343.

title: Curate a suite from a locale: read-side candidate browse, kept out of the graph projection
description:
A curator should be able to pick a locale, see the cards set in it, and assemble a suite from those candidates. The shared slug between `collections` and `locales` (`south-africa` names both, and four seeded cards are in both) makes this ambiguous unless the boundary stays namespaced.

## Why this is not already possible

The graph subsystem cannot serve it today:

- `/api/graph` is read-only by architecture. `trope-cards/test/graph-api.test.ts` asserts POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE return 404, and ADR_GRAPH_LAYER.md lists write paths as deliberately not built.
- Every projection is focus-anchored on a single card. There is no listing, no pagination, and no filter. `trope-cards/src/graph/query.ts` accepts `includeNodeTypes`/`includeEdgeTypes` and nothing else.
- `trope-cards/src/graph/views.ts` has focus projections only, no list/browse view.
- So a curator cannot even enumerate the candidates, let alone assign them.

## Direction (agreed, deferred)

A read-side listing path, deliberately not a write on the projection:

- A new read port method plus route that lists cards in a locale with their current suits, axes and mechanisms, so a curator browses candidates and assembles a suite by hand.
- Reads `trope_graph` only. Never `public.cards`.
- Assignment stays explicit and human. The projection must not infer a locale from a suit or a suit from a locale; `trope-cards/test/graph-projection.test.ts` asserts both directions stay empty.
- Parameter names stay dimension-qualified: `locale=` can never be confused with `suit=`. A bare `slug=` must not resolve across taxonomies.
- If assignment needs a write, it belongs in a separate bounded admin service, not in `/api/graph`, so the read-only guarantee in Issue #3 stays true.

## Already in place

`CardClassification` reports `suitIds` alongside `suits`, mirroring `localeIds`/`mechanismIds`, so a client resolves a shared slug by id rather than by guessing. `graph-locale.integration.test.ts` asserts the shared slug resolves to two different rows in the real database.

## Open questions for whoever picks this up

- Is the curation surface a host-server route, or authoring-time validation in `validate-draft.mjs`?
- Does suite assignment need to be a runtime write at all, or is authoring-time authoring sufficient?
- Which host component consumes the browse endpoint, given `src/components/admin/CardEditor.tsx` is host-side and Prisma-backed, and no bridge to `trope_graph` may be introduced.

title: B2 — Decide the fate of `claim_relations`
description:
Blocking issue from `trope-cards/docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §8 B2. Decision recorded in §12 Q1.

## Problem

`claim_relations` has a full schema — an 11-value `claim_relation_type` enum (SUPPORTS, CHALLENGES,
QUALIFIES, CONTRADICTS, CONTEXTUALISES, EXEMPLIFIES, REQUIRES, GENERALISES, EQUATES,
ANACHRONISTICALLY_MAPS, RETROSPECTIVELY_IDENTIFIES), indexes, and FKs — and **0 rows and no writer**.
No seeder, validator, or test inserts into it.

So the claim↔claim relations named in `ADR_GRAPH_LAYER.md` §5 and Issue #3 have no representable
data. The only current carrier of retrospective/anachronistic mapping is
`inference_steps.inference_type`, which is a different proposition: it records how a conclusion was
reached, not that one claim stands in relation to another.

The v1 projection reads `claim_relations` exactly as authored and never infers claim relations from
inference structure. That is correct but means the claim-relation vocabulary is currently
unreachable from the API.

## This is the biggest open ontology question in Issue #3

Deciding this determines whether claim↔claim SUPPORTS / QUALIFIES / ANACHRONISTICALLY_MAPS /
RETROSPECTIVELY_IDENTIFIES edges exist in the domain at all.

## Options

1. Populate `claim_relations` and make it first-class. Author rows for the identity-retrojection
   cluster, where retrospective identification is the actual editorial claim.
2. Retire it as duplicative of the inference-step model, and document that
   `inference_steps.inference_type` is the sole carrier.

Option 1 risks encoding an inference as a relation between two claims — exactly what Q1 forbids the
projection from doing automatically, but which an author could do by hand. Option 2 loses the
vocabulary but removes the ambiguity.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decision is recorded in `docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §11 Q1.
- Either `claim_relations` has authored rows with an idempotent seeder and a validator, or the
  tables are dropped in a migration and the ADR updated.
- `verify-seed.ts` covers the table so the state is checked by the seed gate.
- If kept: no `claim_relations` row duplicates an `inference_steps` edge. A validator should reject
  a row that merely restates an authored inference.
- If dropped: `docs/ADR_GRAPH_LAYER.md` §5 no longer lists claim relations as a vocabulary.
- The projection is unchanged either way — it already reads the table as authored.

Remove Lovable branding and the gpteng CDN script from index.html
description:
Found while reconciling deployment for GitHub Issue #4. The production HTML that Vite emits still carries its scaffold origin:

```html
<title>truth-tarot-cards</title>
<meta name="description" content="Lovable Generated Project" />
<meta name="author" content="Lovable" />
<!-- IMPORTANT: DO NOT REMOVE THIS SCRIPT TAG OR THIS VERY COMMENT! -->
<script src="https://cdn.gpteng.co/gptengineer.js" type="module"></script>
```

Confirmed in the built bundle: `dist/index.html` serves this to production on every page load.

Three separate concerns:

1. **Third-party script in production.** `cdn.gpteng.co/gptengineer.js` is loaded from a third-party CDN on every page view, with no SRI hash and no `crossorigin` attribute. It executes with full page privileges. Whether or not it is still needed, loading it in production should be a deliberate decision, not scaffold residue.
2. **Wrong project identity.** The title says `truth-tarot-cards`; the application is `as-truth-cards` / "As Truth Cards". The description and author metadata advertise the generator, not the project.
3. **The comment is a trap.** "DO NOT REMOVE THIS SCRIPT TAG OR THIS VERY COMMENT!" invites future maintainers to preserve something nobody has re-evaluated.

Related, left alone as out of scope: `lovable-tagger` is a devDependency imported at the top level of `vite.config.ts` and applied when `mode === 'development'`. It is a build-time tool with no deployment role, but it must stay installed for the Vite config to load at all.

## Acceptance criteria

- `index.html` carries the real project name and description, and no generator branding.
- The `gptengineer.js` script is removed, or gated so it cannot ship to production.
- If the script is kept, the reason is written down and the comment claiming it must not be removed is deleted.
- The title matches `server/auth.ts`'s `appName` and the README.
- `pnpm run build` still succeeds and `dist/index.html` reflects the change.

title: B4 — Document the deliberate decoupling of status vocabularies
description:
Blocking issue from `trope-cards/docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §8 B4. Decision recorded in §12 Q4.

## Problem

`status` is modelled inconsistently across the ontology:

| Location | Type |
|---|---|
| `cards.epistemic_status`, `claims.epistemic_status` | `epistemic_status` enum |
| `inference_steps.inference_status`, `argument_chains.status` | same-named **`text`**, no vocabulary |
| `evidence_items.evidence_status` | `text`, **no vocabulary at all** |
| `inference_steps.is_canonical` | `boolean` |
| lifecycle | four unrelated enums (`case_status`, `question_status`, `relationship_status`, `contribution_status`) |

So a projection offering one graph-wide status filter or rollup would be unsound. `evidence_status`
in particular has no controlled vocabulary at all — the only part of the ontology where a status is
not even an enum.

## Current mitigation

The v1 projection exposes status **per node type** only and offers no graph-wide status field. The
invariant suite asserts each node carries the status field belonging to its own type and no other.

Per `docs/EVIDENCE_LAYER.md`, "never collapse these" is an explicit documented rule, so decoupling
may well be intentional rather than a defect. That is exactly why this issue is about
**documentation**, not unification.

## This issue decides

Whether the decoupled model is deliberate and should be documented as such, or whether
`inference_steps` / `argument_chains` should migrate onto the `epistemic_status` enum.

Unifying is the wrong move for evidence: epistemic confidence, evidence strength, and lifecycle
progress are genuinely different axes, and collapsing them loses information. But a bare `text`
column with no vocabulary is not defensible either — it can hold any string, including a
misspelling.

## Options

1. Treat the decoupling as intentional. Document it in `ADR_GRAPH_LAYER.md`, and give every `text`
   status column an enum or a documented `CHECK` constraint — especially `evidence_status`, which
   currently has no vocabulary whatsoever.
2. Unify `inference_steps` / `argument_chains` onto `epistemic_status`, keeping lifecycle and
   evidence separate.

Option 1 is recommended: it preserves the intentional separation while fixing the real defect, which
is unenforced vocabulary rather than the number of vocabularies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decision is recorded in `docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §11 Q4.
- Every status column in the schema is either an enum or has a documented vocabulary and a
  constraint that enforces it.
- `evidence_items.evidence_status` in particular gains a documented vocabulary.
- `docs/ADR_GRAPH_LAYER.md` states which statuses may be compared and which may not.
- The projection's per-type status contract is unchanged.

title: Fail fast on a missing BETTER_AUTH_SECRET instead of using Better Auth's published default
description:
Found while reconciling `render.yaml` for GitHub Issue #4. `server/auth.ts` does not read `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` itself; Better Auth does, and substitutes a hardcoded default when it is unset:

```js
// better-auth/dist/context/create-context.mjs
secret = legacySecret || "better-auth-secret-12345678901234567890"
```

That constant is published in Better Auth's source. Verified on this repository: with `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` unset and `NODE_ENV=production`, the server binds its port, `GET /health` returns 200, and `GET /api/auth/get-session` returns 200. Nothing warns. `validateSecret` exists but its production branch does not catch this substitution path.

Session cookies are signed with the secret, so a known key means a forgeable session cookie — including one carrying the `ADMIN` role defined in `prisma/schema.prisma`. This is an authentication bypass, not an outage, so no health check will surface it.

`render.yaml` now declares the variable with `generateValue: true`, which closes it for the Render deployment, and the README explains the risk. But any other deployment path, or a blueprint edit that drops the variable, silently reintroduces it.

## Proposed fix

Assert the secret at startup in `server/index.ts` or `server/auth.ts`:

```ts
if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' && !process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET) {
  throw new Error(
    'BETTER_AUTH_SECRET must be set in production. Better Auth falls back to a ' +
    'hardcoded default that is published in its source, which makes session ' +
    'cookies forgeable. Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 32',
  )
}
```

Make it unconditional rather than production-only if that is preferable: the default is wrong in every environment, and local development already sets the variable in `.env`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A missing `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` stops the process with an actionable message, or is otherwise impossible to reach Better Auth's default.
- A test covers the unset case.
- The README and `.env.example` still describe the variable and how to generate one.

title: typecheck:all fails on 8 pre-existing host UI type errors
description:
## Problem

`pnpm run typecheck:all` fails with 8 type errors in the host app. The
Trope Graph work is unaffected — `typecheck:graph` and
`trope-graph:check` are both clean, and the failures predate that work.
Found while wiring the graph into the root tsconfig; recorded in commit
2f31a99 so the green graph check is not mistaken for a green repo.

## Errors

    src/components/ui/resizable.tsx(9,4):   TS2833: Cannot find namespace 'React'. Did you mean 'preact'?
    src/components/ui/resizable.tsx(25,4):  TS2833: Cannot find namespace 'React'. Did you mean 'preact'?
    src/components/ui/skeleton.tsx(6,4):    TS2833: Cannot find namespace 'React'. Did you mean 'preact'?
    src/components/ui/sonner.tsx(4,21):     TS2833: Cannot find namespace 'React'. Did you mean 'preact'?
    src/components/ui/badge.tsx(30,18):     TS2339: Property 'className' does not exist on type 'BadgeProps'
    src/components/ui/sheet.tsx(62,37):     TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to '"bottom" | "left" | "right" | "top"'
    src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx(562,51):  TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type '"default" | "outline"'
    src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx(562,60):  TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type '"default" | "sm" | "lg"'

## Root cause: three separate problems

1. **preact `jsxImportSource` vs an absent `React` global.** This is the
   real cause of the 4 TS2833 errors and the reason they cluster. The
   `ui/` components are shadcn components written for React, and they
   use the ambient `React` namespace without importing it:

       // resizable.tsx:9
       }: React.ComponentProps<typeof ResizablePrimitive.PanelGroup>) => (

   That ambient namespace comes from `@types/react`, which is **not
   installed**. `tsconfig.app.json` sets `"jsxImportSource": "preact"`,
   so TS resolves the `React` hint to preact and refuses.

   `package.json` declares both `preact ^10.29.0` and `react ^18.3.1`
   but no `@types/react`, so `react` ships untyped.

2. **`BadgeProps` is missing `className`.** Independent of preact. The
   interface at badge.tsx:26 does not extend a props type that carries
   `className`, yet line 30 destructures it. Compare the sibling
   components, which spread a `React.HTMLAttributes`-style base.

3. **String-to-literal-union narrowing.** Independent of preact. sheet
   and sidebar accept a `string` where cva variants expect a literal
   union, so the value has to be narrowed or typed as the union.

## Notes

- `noImplicitAny`, `strictNullChecks`, and `noUnusedLocals` are all off in
  the root tsconfig, so this is not a strictness migration. It is three
  genuine type errors.
- Deciding between "install @types/react" and "rewrite these components
  against preact" is a project-level call about which React surface is
  authoritative. Worth settling deliberately rather than installing
  @types/react reflexively — preact and React types are not drop-in
  equivalent, and adding @types/react may surface further errors.

title: Production start command depends on tsx, which is a devDependency
description:
Found while reconciling `render.yaml` for GitHub Issue #4.

The production start command executes TypeScript directly:

- `render.yaml`: `startCommand: pnpm run start`
- `package.json`: `"start": "tsx server/index.ts"`

`tsx` is a **devDependency**. There is no server-side compile step, so the running process needs a dev-time tool. That is fine today — Render installs devDependencies by default, and `NODE_ENV=production` alone does not make npm or pnpm omit them — but it means the deployment is one flag away from failing to boot:

- any `pnpm install --prod`, `--omit=dev`, or `NODE_ENV=production npm ci` step,
- a future `dependencies` optimisation pass,
- a base image or CI change that prunes devDependencies.

The failure would be a start command that cannot find `tsx`, i.e. the service never binds a port.

## Options

1. **Compile the server.** Add a build step emitting JS, and start with `node`. Removes the runtime dev-tool dependency entirely and is the standard production shape. Largest change: the server uses `.js` extensions in imports already, so ESM output should work, but it needs a build entry and verification that `dist/` for the client and the server output do not collide.
2. **Move `tsx` to `dependencies`.** One-line change, keeps the current behaviour. Costs a production install of a tool that is really a build-time convenience, but makes the start command self-sufficient.
3. **Document the constraint and pin it.** Keep the status quo, but make `--frozen-lockfile` and the absence of `--prod` an explicit, enforced part of the deploy contract.

Option 2 is the cheap correct fix; option 1 is the right end state.

Note that `vite.config.ts` also imports `lovable-tagger`, a devDependency, at module scope — a separate but related reason the build needs devDependencies present.

## Acceptance criteria

- The production start path does not silently depend on a devDependency, or the dependency on it is enforced and documented.
- A production build/start is verified in CI, not only locally.

title: Render: free plan silently skips preDeployCommand, so migrations must be run by hand
description:
DECIDED 2026-10-05: stay on the free plan; hand-run migrations. Do not upgrade.

What changed: render.yaml now declares plan: free (was starter) and region: ohio (was oregon), matching the live service so applying the blueprint no longer silently changes billing. README gained a 'Free-tier deploys: migrations are manual' section with the three commands (pnpm run db:migrate:deploy; pnpm run trope-graph:migrate -- --allow-remote; TROPE_GRAPH_ALLOW_REMOTE=1 pnpm run trope-graph:seed), the trigger conditions, and a symptom-to-cause table. render.yaml carries an inline copy of the commands. A 'Build notes' subsection documents both build traps.

Accepting the cost: on free, a green deploy proves only that the build succeeded and the process started. Schema drift is invisible until an endpoint misbehaves. Mitigation is the README symptom table, not automation.

Two build traps found and fixed (both were live service config, neither is a free-tier issue):
1. buildCommand used ';' between install and build, so the build ran even when install failed, producing a bundle from a half-installed node_modules instead of a clean failure. Now '&&'.
2. render.yaml's declared command began with 'corepack enable', which CANNOT run on Render: corepack unlinks /usr/bin/pnpm to install its shim and fails with 'EROFS: read-only file system', breaking the build before anything else runs. Applying the blueprint as written failed two consecutive deploys. Render's image already provides pnpm on PATH. Fixed in both render.yaml and the live service; build verified green.

Still open when the plan is revisited: upgrading to starter is a one-line change in render.yaml and re-enables the pre-deploy chain with no code change needed.

title: Add buildCommand && chain on the live Render service
description: The live buildCommand is 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; pnpm run build' - a ';' separator means 'pnpm run build' runs even when the install fails, so a broken lockfile install produces a build against a half-installed node_modules instead of a clean failure. render.yaml already declares the correct '&&' chain including 'corepack enable'. Fold into the blueprint reconciliation issue.

title: B5 — Resolve the competing claim→source attachment paths
description:
Blocking issue from `trope-cards/docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §8 B5. Decision recorded in §12 Q4.
Blocks the `evidence` view only; not a v1 blocker (0 rows today).

## Problem

A source can be attached to a claim through **four** different tables:

- `claim_sources` — claim→source directly, with `quote_or_excerpt` and `page_reference`
- `interpretation_sources` — interpretation→source
- `question_sources` — question→source
- `evidence_sources` — evidence→source

`claim_sources` bypasses the located-passage model entirely: it records that a source backs a claim
without recording *where* in the source the support is. `docs/EVIDENCE_LAYER.md` explicitly says
do not use `claim_sources` when the passage is known — but the table remains, is nullable-relationship
varied, and has `relationship NOT NULL` while three sibling columns are nullable.

The `evidence` view therefore has no unambiguous claim→source path. The projection cannot decide
which of two populated paths is authoritative.

## Why it is not a v1 blocker

`sources`, all five `evidence_*` tables, and `claim_sources` have 0 rows. The v1
`card-argument-taxonomy` view emits no Source or Evidence node, so the ambiguity is not yet
reachable. It becomes a blocker the moment the evidence corpus is populated.

## Options

1. Deprecate `claim_sources`: when a passage is known, use the evidence model. Keep the table for
   genuinely passage-less attachments, and document that rule.
2. Retire `claim_sources` outright and require all claim→source support to go through evidence.

Option 1 is safer for the existing corpus, which has no evidence rows at all, so a hard retirement
would have no replacement path.

## Also fold in

The eight "how are these related" columns (`claim_sources.relationship`, `interpretation_sources.relationship`,
`card_concepts.relationship`, plus four evidence `relation` columns) have differing nullability and
defaults and no shared vocabulary. Whichever option is chosen should reconcile them.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decision is recorded in `docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §11 Q4 and in `docs/EVIDENCE_LAYER.md`.
- `claim_sources` is either dropped or carries a documented rule for when it may be used.
- The `relationship` columns have a shared, enforced vocabulary, or are consolidated.
- The `evidence` view can resolve claim→source unambiguously, with a test asserting it.

B3 — Harden `relationships` referential integrity
description:
Blocking issue from `trope-cards/docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §8 B3. Decision recorded in §12 Q5.

## Problem

`relationships` is polymorphic with no referential integrity:

- `from_entity_type` / `to_entity_type` are free `text`, not an enum.
- `from_entity_id` / `to_entity_id` are plain uuids with **no foreign keys**.

A reader cannot verify that an endpoint exists, nor that a `*_entity_type` string names a real type.
All 11 live rows happen to be `CARD→CARD`, so the table is safe today and unsafe the moment someone
inserts `CLAIM→CONCEPT` or a stale uuid.

## Current mitigation (in the v1 projection)

A `relationships` row becomes an edge **only** when both discriminators are exactly `CARD` and both
uuids resolve to cards. Anything else is dropped and recorded in `meta.warnings[]`. Edges are
additionally re-checked against the emitted node set after traversal, so a relationship to a card
beyond the traversal frontier cannot produce a dangling edge. Integration tests assert this over all
47 seeded cards.

This is deliberately a *reader-side* mitigation. It makes the projection safe without changing the
schema, per the Issue #3 constraint not to modify the database schema. The schema defect remains.

## Options

1. Replace the polymorphic pair with typed FK columns per entity pair (many columns, strong
   integrity, awkward to extend).
2. Introduce an `entity_type` enum for the discriminators and keep the uuids unconstrained.
3. Keep polymorphic, and accept the defensive projection filter as permanent.

Option 1 is the only one that can actually prevent a dangling edge at write time.

## Acceptance criteria

- A decision is recorded in `docs/GRAPH_PROJECTION_DESIGN.md` §11 Q5.
- If hardened: no `relationships` row can be inserted whose endpoints do not exist, enforced by the
  database rather than by application code.
- `from_entity_type` / `to_entity_type` are constrained to known types.
- If option 3 is chosen: the projection's defensive filter stays, is tested, and the trade-off is
  documented in `docs/ADR_GRAPH_LAYER.md`.
- Any orphaned rows are removed or repaired by a migration, and `verify-seed.ts` covers the table.

title: Rotate production Neon DATABASE_URL (exposed in transcripts and in local .env)
description:
P1. Two distinct exposures of the SAME live production Neon credential (ep-...eu-central-1.aws.neon.tech / truthdb). Password confirmed byte-identical across both (sha256 match, 16 chars). Never rotated.

1. GIT HISTORY -- PERMANENT, THE SERIOUS ONE. Commit bf02791 'modded: some dev work' contains a .env with DATABASE_URL pointing at truthdb WITH its password. e61cc9b later removed .env from tracking, so HEAD is clean, but history retains it. Anyone with a clone can recover it with: git show bf02791:.env. Remote is Codeberg (git@codeberg.org-as-truth-cards:ubuntupunk/as-truth-cards.git); repo visibility was NOT verified because gh is unauthenticated. If that Codeberg repo is or was ever public, treat the credential as compromised.

2. LOCAL .env -- DATABASE_URL points at live truthdb rather than a scratch database. Independent risk: any local command defaulting to DATABASE_URL can write to production. assertLocalHost guards the graph tooling, but that is a speed bump, not a boundary.

3. TRANSCRIPT -- the URL was echoed into AI tool output during the 2026-10-05 Render incident.

Rotation steps, in order: (a) rotate the Neon password FIRST -- this invalidates the git-history copy, the .env copy and the transcript copy in one action, and is worth doing even if the repo is private and trusted; (b) update the Render service env var DATABASE_URL and redeploy; (c) repoint local .env at a local/loopback database and keep prod only in the Render service; (d) set TROPE_GRAPH_DATABASE_URL explicitly in .env so the graph client cannot silently fall back to DATABASE_URL.

Optional, only if the repo is or was public: rewrite history to purge the blob (git filter-repo --path .env --invert-paths), force-push, and have every collaborator reclone. Do not skip (a) in favour of this -- rewriting history is not a substitute for rotation, because clones already exist. Note bf02791 also touched 'modded: some dev work', so confirm no other secrets are in that commit before rewriting.

title: Render: live service has drifted from render.yaml blueprint
description:
PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-10-05. The billing/region footgun is gone.

Fixed: render.yaml said plan: starter + region: oregon while the live service ran free + ohio. Applying the blueprint would have silently started charging and moved the region, costing a cold start on the only production database. Both now match reality (free/ohio). Live buildCommand also corrected to match the blueprint (see as-truth-cards-gvn). preDeployCommand, healthCheckPath and the four missing env vars (BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, BETTER_AUTH_URL, NODE_ENV, TROPE_GRAPH_ALLOW_REMOTE) are now configured on the service.

REMAINING: five leftover Lovable-era env vars are still set on the service -- STACK_SECRET_SERVER_KEY, VITE_STACK_PUBLISHABLE_CLIENT_KEY, VITE_STACK_PROJECT_ID, JWKS_URL, VITE_ADMIN_EMAIL. Confirm none is read anywhere in src/ or server/ (note VITE_* are inlined into the client bundle at build time, so a leak there is public), then remove them. This is a prerequisite for the BETTER_AUTH_SECRET rotation, not an independent cleanup.

title: resolveDatabaseUrl treats an empty TROPE_GRAPH_DATABASE_URL as set, not as unset
description:
Found while writing the deployment env-var contract for GitHub Issue #4.

`trope-cards/src/db/url.ts` resolves the connection string with nullish coalescing:

```ts
const url = process.env.TROPE_GRAPH_DATABASE_URL ?? process.env.DATABASE_URL
```

The intent, stated in the function's own doc comment, is that `DATABASE_URL` is a fallback so the graph can share the host application's connection. But `??` only falls through on `null` and `undefined`. An **empty string** is neither, so `TROPE_GRAPH_DATABASE_URL=""` wins, and the function returns `""` while `DATABASE_URL` — a perfectly good connection string — is ignored.

The next stage then fails with a confusing error from `resolveDatabaseConfig` rather than from the missing value.

This is easy to hit: Render and most platforms treat an env var as set once it exists, so a dashboard variable cleared to an empty string, or a `sync: false` variable left blank, produces exactly this state. `TROPE_GRAPH_DATABASE_URL` is optional in the documented contract, which makes the trap easy to fall into.

`??` should be `||`, or the empty string should be rejected with a message naming the variable. A test covering the empty-string case would pin the behaviour.

Not fixed in Issue #4 because that task is scoped to deployment hygiene and this is graph-subsystem connection code. `render.yaml` currently sets only `DATABASE_URL` and documents the empty-string caveat, so the Render deploy path is unaffected.

## Acceptance criteria

- An empty or whitespace-only `TROPE_GRAPH_DATABASE_URL` falls back to `DATABASE_URL`.
- A test asserts the empty-string case.
- The README / `.env.example` wording matches the behaviour.
